newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks sceptical on gold revaluation plan.
newsitem.headline: German banks sceptical on gold revaluation plan.

text.p: Two German banking groups on Tuesday expressed reservations about Bonn's plans to revalue the gold and foreign exchange assets of the Bundesbank, with one expressing outright disapproval of the scheme.
The German cooperative banking group (BVR) said it was against a revaluation of the assets -- which are in the balance sheet at a value well below the market price -- at the moment.

"It is true that this question would pose itself next year if the Bundesbank is required to transfer part of its foreign exchange reserves to the central bank in time for the punctual start of European monetary union," the BVR said in a statement.
"But forcing the Bundesbank into a higher valuation this year, giving the impression the coffers are empty, is to question the central bank's independence," it added.
Calling for Germany's accounts to be brought into order by other means, it called for a budget freeze, saying this could lead to real savings in the budget.

The Deutscher Sparkassen- und Giroverband savings bank association was less openly critical of the overall plan, but said that it must be made absolutely clear how the revalued reserves would be used.

"A possible special profit transfer by the Bundesbank to the federal government as a result of a valuation of its gold reserves at closer to the market price should only be used to pay off debts associated with German unification," the association's chief economist Axel Bertuch-Samuels said.

He added in a statement that this would restore some confidence in Germany which had been lost as a result of the view that German Finance Minister Theo Waigel intended to use the money to reduce the German deficit.

Noting that it was indeed necessary to plan for a revaluation of German assets ahead of the transfer of some assets to the European Central Bank, he commented that the timing had been unfortunate in raising further questions about the health of Bonn's finances and the independence of the bank.
Waigel two weeks ago presented the idea of revaluing Bundesbank assets, saying he would use any special income from the revaluation to reduce Germany's accumulated debt.
The Bundesbank is due to discuss the plans at a meeting on Wednesday.
